get.description:
> ❗️stream/query is currently in maintenance mode.

This endpoint returns the activity feed for specified users.

**Note:** The Query API has a rate limit of 60 queries per hour and a maximum of 5 concurrent queries.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Required if using service account to authenticate request.

parameters.name: distinct_ids
parameters.description: A JSON array as a string representing the `distinct_ids` to return activity feeds for. For example: `["12a34aa567eb8d-9ab1c26f345b67-89123c45-6aeaa7-89f12af345f678"]`

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to begin querying from. This date is inclusive.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to query to. This date is inclusive.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Required if using service account to authenticate request.

distinct_id.description: A unique identifier used to distinguish an individual profile.

distinct_ids.description:
A JSON array of distinct_ids to retrieve profiles for.
Example: `distinct_ids=["id1", "id2"]`

data_group_id.description: The ID of the group key, used when querying group profiles, click [here](https://docs.mixpanel.com/docs/data-structure/group-analytics#exporting-group-profiles-via-api) for more info.

where.description: An expression to filter users (or groups) by. See the [expressions section](/reference/segmentation-expressions) above.

output_properties.description:
A JSON array of names of properties you want returned.
Example: `output_properties=["$last_name", "$email", "Total Spent"]`

This parameter can drastically reduce the amount of data returned by the API when you're not interested in all properties and can speed up queries significantly.

session_id.description: A string id provided in the results of a previous query. Using a session_id speeds up api response, and allows paging through results.

page.description: Which page of the results to retrieve. Pages start at zero. If the "page" parameter is provided and above 0, the session_id parameter must also be provided.

behaviors.description: If you are exporting user profiles using an event selector, you use a `behaviors` parameter in your request. `behaviors` and `filter_by_cohort` are mutually exclusive.

as_of_timestamp.description:
This parameter is only useful when also using `behaviors`.
If you try to export more than 1k profiles using a `behaviors` parameter and you don't included the parameter `as_of_timestamp`, you'll see the following error:

`request for page in uncached query for params`

filter_by_cohort.description:
Takes a JSON object with a single key called `id` whose value is the cohort ID. `behaviors` and `filter_by_cohort` are mutually exclusive.

Example: `filter_by_cohort='{"id":12345}'`

include_all_users.description:
*\*only applicable with `filter_by_cohort` parameter*

`include_all_users=true` (default) include all distinct_ids even if they don’t have a user (or group) profile.

`include_all_users=false` include only distinct_ids with user (or group) profile.

page.description: The page number of the results

page_size.description: The max number of results in a single page.

status.description: Indicates whether the request was successful

total.description: The number of users in the results payload.

$properties.description: The properties associated with the user

get.description: Get data for a funnel. The Query API has a rate limit of 60 queries per hour and a maximum of 5 concurrent queries.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Required if using service account to authenticate request.

parameters.name: funnel_id
parameters.description: The funnel that you wish to get data for.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to begin querying from. This date is inclusive.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to query to. This date is inclusive.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: The number of units (defined by length_unit) each user has to complete the funnel, starting from the time they triggered the first step in the funnel. May not be greater than 90 days. Note that we will query for events past the end of to_date to look for funnel completions. This defaults to the value that was previously saved in the UI for this funnel.

schema.description: The unit applied to the length parameter can be "second", "minute", "hour", or "day". Defaults to the value that was previously saved in the UI for this funnel.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: The number of days you want each bucket to contain. The default value is 1.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: This is an alternate way of specifying interval and can be "day", "week", or "month".

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Return the top property values. Defaults to 255 if not explicitly included. Maximum value 10,000. This parameter does nothing if \"on\" is not specified.

avg_time.description: mean time to convert; null for step 0.

avg_time_from_start.description: time to convert from first step.

step_label.description: same as event OR custom event name

custom_event.description: `true` if the event is a custom event, otherwise key is not present

custom_event_id.description: Only present if the event is a custom event.

get.description: Get the names and funnel_ids of your funnels.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Required if using service account to authenticate request.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Required if using service account to authenticate request.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to begin querying from. This date is inclusive.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to query to. This date is inclusive.

parameters.name: retention_type
parameters.description: Must be either "birth" or "compounded". Defaults to "birth". The “birth” retention type corresponds to first time retention. The “compounded” retention type corresponds to recurring retention. See the [Types of Retention](https://help.mixpanel.com/hc/en-us/articles/360001370146) article for more information.

parameters.name: born_event
parameters.description: The first event a user must do to be counted in a birth retention cohort. Required when retention_type is "birth"; ignored otherwise.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: The event to generate returning counts for. Applies to both birth and compounded retention. If not specified, we look across all events.

parameters.name: born_where
parameters.description: An expression to filter born_events by. See the [expressions section](/reference/segmentation-expressions) above.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: An expression to filter born_events by. See the [expressions section](/reference/segmentation-expressions) above.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: The number of units (can be specified in either days, weeks, or months) that you want per individual bucketed interval. May not be greater than 90 days if days is the specified unit. The default value is 1.

parameters.name: interval_count
parameters.description: The number of individual buckets, or intervals, that are returned; defaults to 1. Note that we include a "0th" interval for events that take place less than one interval after the initial event.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: The interval unit. It can be "day", "week", or "month". Default is "day".

parameters.name: unbounded_retention
parameters.description: A counting method for retention queries where retention values accumulate from right to left, i.e. day N is equal to users who retained on day N and any day after. The default value of false does not perform this accumulation. [Learn more about Counting Method](https://help.mixpanel.com/hc/en-us/articles/360045484191).

get.description:
Every data point sent to Mixpanel is stored as JSON in our data store. The raw export API allows you to download your event data as it is received and stored within Mixpanel, complete with all event properties (including distinct_id) and the exact timestamp the event was fired.
The raw export API has a rate limit of 60 queries per hour, 3 queries per second, and a maximum of 100 concurrent queries. If you exceed the rate limit, a 429 error will be returned.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: Required if using service account to authenticate request.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.description: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to begin querying from. This date is inclusive and interpreted as UTC timezone for projects created after 1 January 2023 and current project timezone for projects created before 11 January 2023.

parameters.name: to_date
parameters.description: The date in yyyy-mm-dd format to query to. This date is inclusive and interpreted as UTC timezone for projects created after 1 January 2023 and current project timezone for projects created before 11 January 2023.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Use this parameter if you want to limit the max number of events to be returned. Value cannot be over 100000.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: The event or events that you wish to get data for, encoded as a JSON array (for example, `["signup","purchase"]`).

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: An expression to filter events by. More info on expression sequence structure can be found [here](/reference/segmentation-expressions)

parameters.name: time_in_ms
parameters.description:
Defaults to `false` which will export event timestamps with second-precision.
Set to `true` to export event timestamps with millisecond-precision.

parameters.name: Accept-Encoding
parameters.description: If set to `gzip` and the response body is > 1400 bytes, the response will be compressed with gzip, and `Content-Encoding` will be set to `gzip`.

200.description: Success. The returned format is one event per line where each line is a valid JSON object, but the full return itself is JSONL.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description: When set to 1 (recommended), Mixpanel will validate the batch and return errors per event that failed.

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The Mixpanel project_id, used to authenticate service account credentials.

properties.title: properties
properties.description: A JSON object containing properties of the event.

time.title: time
time.description: The time at which the event occurred, in seconds or milliseconds since UTC epoch. If the time value is set in the future, it will be overwritten with the current present time at ingestion.

distinct_id.title: distinct_id
distinct_id.description: The unique identifier of the user who performed the event.

$insert_id.title: $insert_id
$insert_id.description: A unique identifier for the event, used for deduplication. Events with identical values for (event, time, distinct_id, $insert_id) are considered duplicates; only the latest ingested one will be considered in queries.

200.description: Authenticated account metadata; response fields are not specified by the public reference.

workspaceId.name: workspace_id
workspaceId.description: The id of the workspace if applicable.

on.name: on
on.description: The property expression to segment the event on. See the [expression to segment](/reference/segmentation-expressions) below.

where.name: where
where.description: An expression to filter events by. See the [expression to segment](/reference/segmentation-expressions) below.

retentionOn.name: on
retentionOn.description: The property expression to segment the second event on. See the [expressions section](/reference/segmentation-expressions) above.

retentionLimit.name: limit
retentionLimit.description: Return the top limit segmentation values. This parameter does nothing if "on" is not specified.

eventName.name: event
eventName.description: The event that you wish to get data for. Note: this is a single event name, not an array.

type.name: type
type.description: The analysis type you would like to get data for - such as general, unique, or average events. Valid values: "general", "unique", or "average".

unit.name: unit
unit.description: This can be "minute", "hour", "day", "week", or "month". It determines the level of granularity of the data you get back. Note that you cannot get hourly uniques.

interval.name: interval
interval.description: The number of "units" to return data for - minutes, hours, days, weeks, or months. 1 will return data for the current unit (minute, hour, day, week or month). 2 will return the current and previous units, and so on. Specify either interval or from_date and to_date.

format.name: format
format.description: The data return format, such as JSON or CSV. Options: "json" (default), "csv".

limit255.name: limit
limit255.description: The maximum number of values to return. Defaults to 255.

propertyName.name: name
propertyName.description: The name of the property you would like to get data for.

limit10.name: limit
limit10.description: The maximum number of properties to return. Defaults to 10.

items.description: All dates we have data for in the response.

allOf.description: If present and equal to 1, Mixpanel will validate the provided records and return a JSON object with per-record error messages for records that fail validation.

LookupTableReceived.description: A 200 response indicates all records were successfully ingested.

LookupTableInvalid.description: A 400 response indicates that some records failed validation.

example.error: Some data points in the request failed validation.

failed_records.message: primary key is required and cannot be blank
invalid row: wrong number of fields

StrictReceived.description: A 200 response indicates all records were successfully ingested.

StrictInvalid.description: A 400 response indicates that some records failed validation.

failed_records.message: 'properties.time' is invalid: must be specified as seconds since epoch

StrictNotFound.description: A 404 response indicates that the entity to replace was not found.

example.error: Lookup table with id 'f077cb07-008a-4955-8a4a-b4c163db3a87' was not found.

StrictTooLarge.description: A 413 response indicates that the payload is too large.

example.error: request exceeds max limit of 2097152 bytes

RateLimitExceeded.description: A 429 response indicates rate limits have been exceeded.

example.error: Project exceeded rate limits. Please retry the request with exponential backoff.

Received.description:
* `1` - One or more objects provided are valid. This does not signify a valid project token or secret.
* `0` - No data objects in the body are valid.
